title: Perceived predation risk increases mobbing intensity in tits
content:
Abstract
Mobbing is a widespread antipredator strategy among prey species and can be considered as a form of cooperation. As such, it is expected to be enhanced when the perceived risk of predation is locally increased. Here, through a manipulation of the landscape of fear (variation in the perceived predation risk 3 min per day), we study how it affects the propensity to engage in mobbing behavior of 2 Paridae species (great tit and blue tit). For our 2 target species, a high perceived risk of predation led to a greater engagement in mobbing behavior. Additionally, we found no difference in mobbing engagement between the 2 species (even though the acoustic stimuli used were only heterospecific for the great tit), suggesting that heterospecific cooperation also increases when the risk of predation increases.
